finding: FramePool mutex locks on every render-frame get/recycle. FramePool::get() and FramePool::recycle() both acquire a std::mutex lock on every call. These are invoked on the render hotpath — GlobalPool::getFramePool().recycle(frame) is called in playercore.cpp:802 for every rendered frame, and get() is called by AudioOutput::resampleFrameToBuffer on every SDL callback fill cycle. Locking a mutex per frame introduces unpredictable latency spikes on both the render and audio fill paths. The SPSC design of the pool is undermined by the shared mutex — this is a hotpath blocker.
mitigation: Replace the mutex with a lock-free SPSC queue (e.g., ring buffer of AVFrame pointers). The design should be single-producer (decode/render threads) or single-consumer (audio callback). Alternatively, use a thread-local pool per thread so no cross-thread synchronization is needed at all.

finding: PacketPool mutex locks on demux hotpath. PacketPool::get() and PacketPool::recycle() both take a std::mutex lock on every call. get() is called by the demux thread at playercore.cpp:561,646 to get a packet slot, and recycle() is called by decode threads to return packets. This is on the hotpath of every packet processed. Since packets flow strictly demux to decode (single producer, single consumer), no mutex is needed — a lock-free SPSC structure would eliminate all contention.
mitigation: Replace with a lock-free SPSC structure (e.g., a custom atomic ring buffer or lock-free MPMC queue). The demux thread is the sole producer and the decode threads are consumers — a ring buffer of AVPacket pointers with atomic head/tail indices is sufficient and eliminates all mutex overhead.

finding: audio_clock_us_ cross-thread data race. audio_clock_us_ is written at audiooutput.cpp:220 inside resampleFrameToBuffer(), which is called from the SDL audio callback — a high-frequency real-time audio thread. It is read at syncclock.h:183 via get_audio_clock() (called from the main thread through playercore.cpp:963) and at syncclock.h:136 inside calc_display_delay() (called from the video render thread at playercore.cpp:718). The write in resampleFrameToBuffer() does not hold a lock. calc_display_delay() reads m_audio_clock at line 136 without a mutex. get_audio_clock() uses a lock but is called from the main thread, not the audio thread. This creates a confirmed data race across SDL audio thread, video render thread, and main thread.
mitigation: Make audio_clock_us_ and m_audio_clock atomic. Use std::atomic<int64_t> for the audio clock value so cross-thread reads/writes are safe without mutex overhead on the real-time audio path. Alternatively, ensure set_audio_clock() uses a mutex and that calc_display_delay() also locks when reading m_audio_clock — but std::atomic is preferred for the hotpath.

finding: currentSubtitle_ cross-thread write/read without synchronization. currentSubtitle_ (a QString) is written from the video render thread via uploadSubtitleTexture() at line 394, which is called from a signal handler on that thread. It is read in paintGL() at line 252, which runs on the Qt GUI/main thread. No mutex or atomic guards this member. subTitleWidth_ and subTitleHeight_ have the same cross-thread access pattern. This is a confirmed data race between the video render thread and the GUI thread.
mitigation: Guard writes/reads of currentSubtitle_, subTitleWidth_, and subTitleHeight_ with a QMutex, or make the width/height values QAtomicInteger-backed. Alternatively, ensure the subtitleReady signal is delivered via Qt::QueuedConnection so the write always happens on the main thread event loop — though a mutex is more robust against races if paintGL races with a concurrent signal delivery.

finding: AVSyncClock data race — calc_display_delay() reads members without mutex. calc_display_delay() (called from the video render thread at playercore.cpp:718) reads m_last_pts, m_last_delay, m_frame_timer, m_lag_count, and m_audio_clock without holding m_mutex. These members are written from within calc_display_delay() itself and from set_audio_clock() (which holds the mutex). The need_force_catch_up() at line 161 reads m_last_pts and m_audio_clock without a lock. Simultaneously, audiooutput.cpp:222 calls set_audio_clock() which writes m_audio_clock under the mutex. The hotpath video render thread reads without locking while the audio thread writes under locking — a data race.
mitigation: Make m_audio_clock, m_last_pts, m_last_delay, m_frame_timer, and m_lag_count all std::atomic<int64_t> or std::atomic<int> so that cross-thread reads/writes are safe without mutex overhead on the hotpath. The m_mode, m_has_audio, m_has_video, and m_speed flags can remain non-atomic if set only at initialization and never changed during playback.

finding: AudioOutput::resampleFrameToBuffer leaks audio_buf_ on every call when need_resample_ is false. When need_resample_ is false, the code calls realloc(audio_buf_, audio_buf_size_) inside the while-loop on every Pop(), discarding the previous audio_buf_ pointer without freeing it. realloc can return a new pointer (it does here since audio_buf_size_ changes per frame). The old pointer is lost — a memory leak. Only the final DeInit() path frees audio_buf_. Additionally, at line 184, the same realloc pattern overwrites the pointer before checking the return value — if realloc fails and returns nullptr, the original allocation is permanently leaked.
mitigation: Use a temporary pointer for the realloc result: uint8_t* tmp = (uint8_t*)realloc(audio_buf_, buf_size); if (!tmp) { /* log */ return 0; } audio_buf_ = tmp;. This pattern applies to both the resampling and non-resampling branches (line 202). Better still, use a single pre-allocated buffer with a fixed max capacity and memcpy only when growing, eliminating realloc entirely.

finding: Per-frame QByteArray heap reallocation in video render hotpath. In videoRenderThreadFunc, two local QByteArray variables (yuv_data, rgbData) are constructed as empty and grown frame-by-frame via append() calls inside the per-frame render loop. QByteArray has no capacity reservation, so each append that exceeds the current buffer causes a heap reallocation plus memcpy. At video frame rate (30-60 Hz) this creates a CPU hotspot: realloc amplification, unnecessary heap churn, and extra cache misses. This happens on every rendered frame.
mitigation: Pre-allocate yuv_data and rgbData with reserve() to the known frame buffer size (w*h*3/2 for NV12, w*h*3/2 for YUV420P, w*h*4 for RGBA) before the first append. Alternatively, pass the frame's native AVFrame data pointers directly to the renderer without an intermediate heap copy — the OpenGL texture upload can use FFmpeg's own planes directly via glTexSubImage2D.

finding: SubtitlePopup created with new on every button click — widget leak. on_subtitleBtn_clicked() creates a new SubtitlePopup each time the button is clicked (line 1470). Since SubtitlePopup is a QWidget with Qt::Popup flag, the widget is shown non-modally. When the user dismisses it, there is no delete or ownership transfer — it leaks on every click after the first. Over a playback session with repeated subtitle button clicks, these widgets accumulate.
mitigation: Create subtitlePopup_ once as a member variable of MainWindow (like settingdialog_), and call subtitlePopup_->show() / subtitlePopup_->hide() in the button handler. Alternatively, call setAttribute(Qt::WA_DeleteOnClose) on the dialog before show().

finding: Multiple classes missing Q_DISABLE_COPY_MOVE — implicit copies of mutex-bearing and raw-pointer-owning classes. AVSyncClock (has mutable QMutex), PlayerCore (owns raw pointers to demuxer/decoder/thread, has QMutex), PreviewPlayer (owns Demuxer*, Decoder*, QThread*, QMutex), Demuxer (owns AVFormatContext*, has QReadWriteLock), and AsrWorker (owns whisper_context* handle) all lack Q_DISABLE_COPY_MOVE. Accidental copies would duplicate thread handles, double-close AVFormatContext, double-delete decoder pointers, or cause double-free of whisper_context, with no compiler warning.
mitigation: Add Q_DISABLE_COPY_MOVE(ClassName) to each class after the Q_OBJECT macro. For AVSyncClock, PlayerCore, PreviewPlayer, Demuxer, and AsrWorker, add Q_DISABLE_COPY_MOVE(AVSyncClock), Q_DISABLE_COPY_MOVE(PlayerCore), etc. This is a one-line fix per class that prevents all accidental copy/move operations.

finding: QMap used for TF-IDF term-frequency counting — O(log n) insert/lookup. QMap<QString, int> tf is used to accumulate term frequencies in tfidfVector(). QMap is a red-black tree with O(log n) insert/lookup. For term-frequency counting over a token list (where duplicate keys are frequent and order is irrelevant), QHash provides O(1) average-case insert/lookup. With thousands of subtitle entries in the ASR post-processing path, the cumulative effect is measurable.
mitigation: Replace QMap<QString, int> tf with QHash<QString, int> tf. The iteration and access patterns (tf[tok]++ and constBegin/constEnd iteration) are identical between QMap and QHash — no other code change is needed. QHash also has better cache locality for the hash table vs. QMap's tree nodes.

finding: O(n) linear scan in addToFileList on every file addition. addToFileList iterates over the entire fileList to find the index of the just-added file via a for loop. Since addToFileList is called once per file addition and fileList grows unboundedly, this is O(n) per insertion — O(n^2) total for loading a large playlist. For a 500-file playlist this means ~125,000 loop iterations vs. a constant-time operation.
mitigation: After fileList.append(filePath), set listIndex = fileList.size() - 1 directly instead of searching. The index is always the newly appended item's position — no search is needed.

finding: Unbounded std::vector::insert in ASR resampling loop — repeated reallocations. In runWhisperASR, std::vector<float> pcm grows via pcm.insert(pcm.end(), ...) at line 627 every 30-second audio segment. std::vector::insert at the end without pre-reservation causes logarithmic reallocations as the vector doubles its capacity. For a 2-hour video with many segments, the vector is reallocated 20+ times, causing unnecessary memcpy of all previously accumulated samples each time.
mitigation: After the demuxer opens the audio file, compute the approximate total samples from demuxer_->getDuration() and sampleRate, then call pcm.reserve() once before the demux loop. Clear and re-reserve after each ASR submit if the vector is reused across segments.

finding: getSpeedFromIndex defined but never called — dead code in central player class. The method getSpeedFromIndex (lines 883-892) computes a playback speed multiplier from a table of 5 entries. This method is defined, compiled, and linked but never invoked anywhere in the codebase. setSpeed calls sync_clock_->setSpeedRatio() directly with a value computed inline via integer index math, bypassing this method entirely. Dead code increases binary size and confuses future maintainers.
mitigation: Either remove getSpeedFromIndex entirely, or wire it into setSpeed and keyPressEvent to centralize the speed-index-to-ratio logic so the table is defined in one place. The latter approach is preferred for maintainability.

finding: Wrong FFmpeg API used for planar vs. packed format buffer size. av_sample_fmt_is_planar(fmt) at line 118 is followed by av_get_packed_size(fmt) at line 120. av_sample_fmt_is_planar tells whether a format is planar, but av_get_packed_size ignores this entirely — it assumes a packed format regardless. For planar formats like FLTP or S16P, av_get_packed_size returns an incorrect size. The correct API is av_samples_get_buffer_size(&linesize, channels, samples, fmt, align), which handles both planar and packed formats correctly.
mitigation: Replace the is_planar / get_packed_size branch with av_samples_get_buffer_size(nullptr, channels, numSamples, fmt, 1), which works correctly for both planar and packed pixel/audio formats. This also simplifies the code by removing the planar/packed branch entirely.

file: core/playercore.h:68-74, utils/picturecreator.h:17-18, resampler/resampler.h:40-43, pool/framepool.h:20, pool/packetpool.h:20, render/audiooutput.h:42,44, filter/audiofilter.h:39-40
finding: get-prefix on plain const getters throughout codebase — Qt naming convention violation. Multiple methods use the 'get' prefix for simple const accessors: getDuration(), getCurrentPos(), getCurrentTimeSec(), getState(), getMediaType(), getAVFormatContext(), getFileUrl() in playercore.h; getDuration() in picturecreator.h; getInputSpec(), getOutputSpec(), getSwrContext(), getOutputBufferSize() in resampler.h; getMaxSize() in both pool headers; getVolume(), getAudioClock() in audiooutput.h; getSpeedValue(), getSpeedIndex() in audiofilter.h. Qt convention reserves 'get' for out-parameter decomposition. These should be bare names matching the field (e.g., duration(), state(), volume()).
mitigation: Rename each get*() method to an unprefixed name across all affected files. Consider adding Q_PROPERTY declarations for playercore.h getters if the class needs to expose properties to QML or Qt property bindings. A global search-and-replace is straightforward since the names are consistent.

finding: Unscoped enums without explicit underlying type. Three enums in the codebase are unscoped (classic style) without an explicit underlying type: LogLevel in utils/log.h, RowType in summary/transcriptpanel.h, and SpeedIndex in filter/audiofilter.h. In C++11+ this defaults to int, which is ABI-compatible but implicit conversions can silently produce unexpected results. Modern C++ guidelines recommend either enum class (strongly typed) or an explicit enum : int for classic enums.
mitigation: Convert to enum class for strong type safety (enum class LogLevel : int, enum class RowType : int, enum class SpeedIndex : int), or add explicit underlying types (enum LogLevel : int). This requires updating any switch statements that use these enums to handle the scoped enumerators (e.g., LogLevel::LOG_DEBUG instead of LOG_DEBUG), but the switch statements already have default: labels so they are resilient to new enumerators.

finding: av_malloc/av_free mismatch and uninitialized pointer free in AsrRealtimeStrategy::sendAudio. av_malloc allocates buf at line 64, but av_free is used to release it at line 70. FFmpeg's av_malloc allocates with alignment and metadata — av_free is technically safe here (it calls av_freep internally), but this is an API misuse pattern. More critically, if resample fails or returns 0 samples, av_free(buf) is still called on a potentially uninitialized pointer, which could be a no-op but is fragile. Per-frame malloc/free for the audio buffer also creates unnecessary allocation overhead on the ASR audio path.
mitigation: Use av_mallocz + av_freep consistently, or better yet, switch to a pre-allocated reusable buffer in the ring buffer to avoid per-frame allocation/free cycles entirely. Add a null check before av_free(buf) if the per-frame allocation pattern is kept.

finding: ShotCutDialog and VideoInfoDialog created in contextMenuEvent with new and no ownership. Both dialogs are new'd in contextMenuEvent and .show()n, but never stored or explicitly deleted. ShotCutDialog is given 'this' as parent so Qt will delete it when MainWindow is destroyed, but since MainWindow lives for the entire application session, dialogs accumulate in memory with each right-click. VideoInfoDialog has no parent specified, meaning it must be explicitly deleted — but no delete exists.
mitigation: Either store both dialogs as member variables of MainWindow and reuse them, or call setAttribute(Qt::WA_DeleteOnClose) on each dialog before .show(). This ensures one dialog instance per right-click and proper cleanup when closed.

finding: VideoSummaryManager m_networkBridge relies on implicit parent deletion — potential leak on normal completion. m_networkBridge is created with m_workerThread as parent (new SummaryNetworkBridge(m_networkClient, m_workerThread) at line 82). The destructor deletes m_networkClient but relies on the QObject parent hierarchy for m_networkBridge deletion. The comment at line 114 says 'Qt 会自动 delete bridge'. However, if the summary completes normally (line 463 sets state to Finished without calling stopSummary), the worker thread may not be explicitly stopped and the bridge may leak. Additionally, m_networkBridge is set to nullptr without a delete, relying on parent-child destruction order.
mitigation: Ensure stopSummary() is called in the destructor even on Finished state, or add explicit delete m_networkBridge in the normal completion path after setState(Finished). Verify the QThread parent-child relationship correctly covers the bridge's lifetime in all exit paths.

finding: m_asrResults mutated from worker thread and delivered via signal without explicit connection type. runWhisperASR() (line 551, worker thread) appends to m_asrResults at lines 637 and 648, then emits asrCompleted(m_asrResults) at line 659. The receiver TranscriptPanel::setSubtitleItems() runs on the main thread. A comment at line 656 claims the cross-thread safety is via Qt::QueuedConnection, but the connection type is not explicitly specified in runWhisperASR. Relying on implicit connection type (which defaults to Qt::AutoConnection) is fragile — if the signal is emitted from the same thread as the receiver at the time of emission, it becomes DirectConnection and crosses threads unsafely.
mitigation: Explicitly specify the connection type when connecting asrCompleted: connect(this, &VideoSummaryManager::asrCompleted, receiver, &TranscriptPanel::setSubtitleItems, Qt::QueuedConnection). Also protect m_asrResults mutations with m_mutex in the worker thread as a defensive measure, since the vector is also cleared/read from other code paths.

finding: Demuxer::seek() accesses fmtCtx_->streams[streamIdx] without holding lock. seek() at line 134 accesses fmtCtx_->streams[streamIdx] directly without acquiring lock_ (the write lock used by open() and close()). The commented-out QWriteLocker at line 123 hints at awareness of this issue. If seek is called while readPacket() holds a QReadLocker, and another thread is mid-destruction of fmtCtx_ in close(), this is a race. The demux thread holds a read lock while the main thread (via PlayerCore::seek at line 385) calls seek() without a lock.
mitigation: Add a QWriteLocker inside seek() to acquire lock_ before accessing fmtCtx_->streams. Alternatively, use a separate QMutex dedicated to seeking that is acquired alongside the read lock. Ensure the fmtCtx_ pointer itself is stable — the readPacket path also accesses fmtCtx_ without a write lock, so a shared seek mutex that both paths acquire would solve the race entirely.

finding: open() in QtConcurrent::run emits signals from pooled thread. PlayerCore::open() for network URLs uses QtConcurrent::run to execute openInternal() on a pooled thread, then emits openResult(ret), playFailed(info), and initFinished() from that pooled thread. Qt delivers these via Qt::QueuedConnection by default for cross-thread signals, but the thread pool affinity of QtConcurrent::run is not as predictable as a dedicated QThread — the signals will be delivered eventually but the thread pool workers are shared, making debugging and resource management harder. The signals carry trivially-copyable types so there is no memory safety issue, but the thread model is non-deterministic.
mitigation: Use a dedicated QThread (or QThreadPool with a specific QRunnable) instead of QtConcurrent::run, so thread affinity is explicit and predictable. If QtConcurrent::run is preferred for simplicity, move signal emissions back to the main thread using QMetaObject::invokeMethod with Qt::QueuedConnection inside the QtConcurrent lambda.

finding: AsrRealtimeStrategy::running_ plain bool written from main thread, read from ASR thread. running_ is set in stop() (called from the main thread via AsrManager::stop() and PlayerCore::stop() at line 298) and read in run() at line 79 (ASR worker thread). This is a cross-thread bool write/read without std::atomic. On most platforms a bool write is atomic, but the C++ standard only guarantees atomicity for std::atomic<bool>, and without it the compiler may optimize by caching the value in a register on the ASR thread.
mitigation: Change AsrRealtimeStrategy::running_ to std::atomic<bool> so that the stop signal from the main thread is safely visible to the ASR thread without undefined behavior. This is a one-line type change that fixes the data race.

finding: getStreamIndex called on every packet in demux hotpath — redundant mutex acquisitions. Inside demuxThreadFunc, both getStreamIndex(AVMEDIA_TYPE_AUDIO) and getStreamIndex(AVMEDIA_TYPE_VIDEO) are called on every packet iteration. Each call acquires a QReadLocker, walks the stream array, and returns an integer. These values never change between openInternal and close. This means thousands of redundant mutex acquisitions per second in the demux hotpath.
mitigation: Cache audio_stream_idx_ and video_stream_idx_ as const int member variables of PlayerCore. Initialize them once in openInternal after the demuxer opens, and use the cached values directly in demuxThreadFunc. No mutex acquisition needed since the values are immutable after initialization.

finding: saveFrameToImage creates SwsContext without RAII — early return path leaks. sws_getContext is called at line 841 to create a SwsContext for frame-to-image conversion. It is freed at line 876 via sws_freeContext only at the normal end of the function. If any subsequent operation (sws_scale, QImage construction, or img.save) fails and causes an early return, sws_freeContext is never called and the SwsContext leaks. Specifically, if the format is unrecognized (e.g., AV_PIX_FMT_NONE), the function falls through without freeing sws_ctx_.
mitigation: Use a RAII wrapper for SwsContext: std::unique_ptr<SwsContext, decltype(&sws_freeContext)> sws_ctx(sws_getContext(...), sws_freeContext);. This guarantees sws_freeContext is called on all return paths, including early returns and exceptions. No other code change is needed.

finding: QJsonValue::toString() used without isString() guard on AI API responses. QJsonValue::toString() silently returns an empty QString for both missing keys and keys with non-string values (null, numbers, etc.). The code uses chained .toString() calls on the AI API response without first calling isString(), making it impossible to distinguish a missing field error from a malformed value. If the API returns a non-2xx status, the JSON body may contain {"error": {"message": "..."}} but the code only checks resp.contains("error") at line 71 and ignores it, falling through to the choices path and potentially producing an empty or malformed result.
mitigation: Add if (!val.isString()) { qWarning() << "Expected string field:" << key; } guards before each critical .toString() extraction, especially for the AI API response chain at lines 202, 270, and 399. Consider using a helper function that returns an optional QString or logs a detailed error on unexpected JSON structure.

finding: Magic number 100 as volume scale constant in hot audio callback path. float factor = volume_ / 100.0f uses a bare literal 100.0f for the volume scale. This constant represents the max volume level and is used in applyVolume() on every SDL audio callback fill cycle (~1000x per second). If the volume range ever changes (e.g., to 0-255 or 0-1), every occurrence of this literal must be found and replaced manually across the codebase.
mitigation: Define static constexpr int kMaxVolume = 100; at AudioOutput class scope and use it in the computation: volume_ / (float)kMaxVolume. No performance impact — the compiler constant-folds this. This makes the relationship between volume_ and the scale explicit and maintainable.

finding: sws_getContext return value not checked before use in SwsContext hot path. sws_getContext can return nullptr if the parameters are invalid (e.g., zero width/height, unsupported pixel format). At videoconverter.cpp:57, the return value is not assigned or checked. The subsequent sws_scale call at line 83 uses sws_ctx_ directly, which could be null, leading to a crash. The same pattern appears in playercore.cpp:841 where sws_getContext is also called without a null check.
mitigation: Null-check sws_ctx_ after sws_getContext and return false or log a fatal error on failure. Consider wrapping SwsContext in a RAII type (std::unique_ptr<SwsContext, decltype(&sws_freeContext)>) that is automatically freed on destruction, eliminating manual sws_freeContext calls throughout the codebase.

finding: whisper_full return value unchecked — silent failure on ASR error. AsrWorker::getText() calls whisper_full() synchronously and waits for completion. whisper_full() returns an int (0 on success). If Whisper returns a non-zero error code (e.g., due to invalid audio format, model load failure, or silent audio), the error is silently ignored and the function waits indefinitely for output that will never arrive. There is no timeout and no error propagation back to the caller.
mitigation: Check whisper_full return value. On non-zero, emit an error signal or return an empty result with an error flag. Add a timeout mechanism to the future/callback in AsrOfflineStrategy::run() so that a stuck ASR call does not block the worker thread indefinitely.

finding: SDL_PauseAudio(0) called before SDL_OpenAudio — premature unpause with no effect. SDL_PauseAudio(0) is called at line 169 before SDL_OpenAudio at line 170. SDL_PauseAudio(0) resumes the audio device, but no device is open yet — this is a no-op. The actual unpause happens implicitly when SDL_OpenAudio opens the device, or explicitly at line 175 after SDL_OpenAudio succeeds. The pre-open call is misleading and suggests incorrect ordering assumptions.
mitigation: Remove the pre-open SDL_PauseAudio(0) at line 169. Keep only the post-open call at line 175 (or move it directly after SDL_OpenAudio with a comment explaining the ordering).

finding: av_image_fill_arrays and av_image_alloc both used in the same decode session. av_image_fill_arrays at line 83 (attach-pool-buffer path) and av_image_alloc at line 106 (allocate path) are both reachable in the same decode session. The second call reallocates or leaks what the first call set up. This creates unpredictable buffer ownership: the first AVFrame from the frame pool gets its buffers set by av_image_fill_arrays, then a second frame is allocated by av_image_alloc, potentially leaking the pool buffer. The decode loop appears to use one path or the other based on a condition, but the inconsistency suggests incomplete understanding of which allocation strategy is actually active.
mitigation: Unify the buffer allocation strategy. Choose either av_image_fill_arrays consistently (for pool-backed frames) or av_image_alloc consistently (for self-allocated frames) per decode session. If pool-backed frames are used, av_image_fill_arrays should be used; if self-allocated frames are used, av_image_alloc should be used — not both in the same code path.

finding: AsrManager::start() returns silently on double-call without error. AsrManager::start() checks if (running_) return; and returns silently if called when already running. In PlayerCore::play(), asr_manager_->start() is called at line 176. If play() is called when playback is already running, start() silently ignores the call with no warning or error return. The caller has no way to know whether ASR actually started, making debugging difficult.
mitigation: Return bool from start() (true if started, false if already running). Log a warning when called redundantly. Alternatively, use Q_ASSERT(!running_) to catch programmer errors in debug builds, combined with a bool return value.

finding: Missing [[nodiscard]] on non-void returning functions throughout codebase. Several non-void returning functions that return important values are not marked [[nodiscard]]. Examples: AVCodecContext* codecCtx() const; in decoder.h:37, MediaType mediaType() const; in demuxer.h:46, and formatContext() in demuxer.h. These functions return raw pointers or values where ignoring the return value would be a programming error. Without [[nodiscard]], the compiler cannot warn if a caller accidentally ignores the return value.
mitigation: Add [[nodiscard]] to high-value functions where ignoring the return is likely a bug: codecCtx(), formatContext(), swrContext(), queue(), segmentAt(), and report(). This is a low-priority hygiene improvement — the compiler will warn on [[nodiscard]] violations in CI but the code is functionally correct without it.

finding: AsrOfflineStrategy accesses queue_ pointer across thread boundary with AsrManager — lifetime risk. AsrOfflineStrategy::run() calls queue_->push() at lines 102 and 111 and queue_->clear() at line 82. queue_ is a raw pointer to AsrManager's queue_ member (set at line 15). SubtitleQueue::push() and clear() both acquire std::mutex so individual operations are thread-safe. However, AsrOfflineStrategy::run() calls queue_->clear() inside the worker thread while AsrManager::stop() (called from main thread) may also call queue_.clear(). While the mutex protects each operation, the queue_ raw pointer itself could dangle if AsrManager is destroyed before the ASR thread fully joins. The ~AsrManager calls stop() which calls strategy_->stop() which does thread_.join() — this ordering appears correct, but the raw pointer coupling is fragile.
mitigation: The join chain appears sound (verified: ~AsrManager calls stop() which calls thread_.join()). The primary risk is the raw pointer coupling. Consider using a shared_ptr to the SubtitleQueue so the queue lives as long as any thread still referencing it, eliminating the dangling pointer risk entirely.
